是否能够成为欲望对象”，而是 B 一旦成为实际情色关系中的他者，是否自动成为 A 的竞争者。齐泽克的论证似乎预设，任何被实际实行的情色关系都会重新把相关人物放入一个共同的选择空间：如果我能够与 B 发生性关系，那么 B 就仍然作为我的某种“可能对象”存在，而 A 因此失去了绝对性。然而，这只有在情色对象与激进爱对象必须属于同一个比较序列的前提下才成立。本文恰恰对这一点提出质疑：一个主体完全可能坚持 A 在爱情、人生承诺和不可替代性上的绝对优先，同时认为 B 在情色层面具有真实意义，却并不因此成为能够替代 A 的候选者。这里不存在逻辑矛盾，除非我们预先规定所有情色关系都会自动进入爱情的竞争结构。因此，本文对齐泽克的反驳并不是自由主义式的“我拥有任何欲望，就有权实现任何欲望”。相反，它接受齐泽克对这种主体模型的大部分批判。本文提出的是一个更加有限的质疑：即使我们承认真正的爱会重新组织主体的欲望空间，也仍然需要独立证明这种重新组织为什么必须采取“所有其他情色可能性均被关闭”这一特定形式。 齐泽克已经说明了为什么爱情需要限制，为什么自由不等于拥有无限选择，以及为什么他人不能被还原为满足不同需求的工具；但这些论证共同支持的是“爱改变主体与其他可能性的关系”，而不是直接证明“爱必须取消一切其他情色关系的现实可能性”。5. 从关系制度到爱的本体论：开放关系是否必然削弱“唯一者”这一理论断点也解释了为什么当代关于非独占关系的讨论虽然能够补充本文，却不能简单替代齐泽克的问题。Elizabeth Brake提出的 amatonormativity 指出，现代社会往往预设每个人都应该追求一个中心的、长期的、排他的浪漫关系，并进一步把这种关系视作成人生活中天然最有价值的亲密形式。Luke Brunning对于 polyamory 的分析则进一步强调，非独占关系并不只是对单偶制约束的简单删除；第三人的出现会改变原本封闭的双人关系动力，并迫使参与者重新处理嫉妒、承诺、边界和情感劳动。这些分析说明“一个中心爱情关系必须同时垄断所有性关系”并非无需解释的普遍人类事实，而具有明显的规范性和制度性背景。然而，齐泽克的理论不能仅仅通过指出 mononormativity 或 amatonormativity 的历史建构性来驳倒。齐泽克完全可以承认单偶制是一种历史制度，同时坚持真正爱情本身在结构上包含某种排他的 cut。换言之，他的论证不是“因为社会一直如此，所以真正的爱必须如此”，而是“真正的爱如果真的改变主体，就必须使一个偶然的人获得绝对地位”。因此，对齐泽克最有效的反驳不是证明非独占关系在社会上也可以运作，而是进一步区分爱的绝对地位与性欲实现的独占权。只有这样，争论才真正进入他的理论内部。萨特与波伏娃著名的“essential love / contingent loves”安排在思想史上提供了一个接近本文问题的先例，但它本身也没有解决这一哲学争论。他们试图让彼此的关系保持一种根本性的优先地位，同时允许其他关系存在；这个安排说明“一个关系具有特殊中心性”与“其他情感或情色关系存在”并非实践上的概念矛盾。但齐泽克仍然可以回应说，这种所谓“essential love”恰恰还没有达到他所说的 radical love，因为它没有让其他可能性真正失效。因此，历史案例最多证明另一种爱情制度可以存在，却无法决定“真正的爱”究竟应该如何定义。最终，本文所捍卫的也不是一种新的普遍关系伦理。它并不主张，当长期爱情中的欲望下降时，人们就应该转向非单偶关系；相反，有些主体完全可能在同一个关系中通过重新遭遇对方的他者性、距离和不可知性，使情色欲望再次出现。另一些主体则可能认为对其他人的欲望无需实行，而恰恰愿意把这种放弃理解为爱情的一部分。本文只拒绝再增加一个未经证明的普遍命题：只有后一种选择才能被称为真正的爱情。从精神分析角度看，不同关系结构甚至可能在不同主体那里承担完全相反的功能。对某个主体而言，非独占关系可能成为避免真正亲密、永远维持幻想对象距离的一种防御；对另一个主体而言，它可能反而减少了要求主要伴侣同时承担所有幻想功能的压力，使主体第一次能够把被爱者看作一个普通、有限而不可替代的人。单偶制也同样如此：它可以成为承担缺失与承诺的形式，也可以成为对伴侣进行占有、幻想融合并否认他者性的方式。因此，关系结构本身不能直接告诉我们主体是否“面对了欲望”。精神分析真正能够提出的问题始终是：这个结构对于这个主体究竟在做什么。6 结论：齐泽克已经证明了爱的“切断”，但尚未证明这种切断必须发生在性欲对象的边界上从弗洛伊德到拉康，爱与欲望之间的问题经历了一次重要的理论变化。弗洛伊德观察到温柔与性欲可能分裂，并倾向于将二者最终在同一对象上的汇合作为成熟性生活的理想形式；拉康则把这种问题转向更根本的结构层面，使爱与欲望不再被理解为两种最终能够完全整合的心理力量，而成为围绕缺失、要求、幻想与他者以不同逻辑运行的关系。爱与欲望因此可以重合，但这种重合没有任何保证；它们也可以发生张力，而这种张力本身不意味着其中一方必须被消灭。在这一背景下，齐泽克做出了一个重要而且有力的伦理推进。他正确指出，不能因为爱与欲望具有不同结构，就把关系理解为一个满足不同心理功能的配置系统。真正的爱不是一个对象满足主体既定需要的结果，而是一种能够重新组织需要本身的事件；也正因如此，真正的自由可以表现为对某些可能性的主动放弃，而不是对所有欲望都保持实现通道。这一批评有效地阻止了一种过于轻率的非独占关系辩护，即“一人无法满足全部需要，所以应该让不同人分别满足不同需要”。然而，这一批评若要进一步证明性单偶制是激进之爱的必要条件，仍然必须完成最后一步。齐泽克需要证明：只要一个主体允许对 B 的情色欲望进入实际关系，A 就已经不再能够成为激进之爱的唯一者。 这个命题既不能从拉康关于欲望的缺失结构中推出，也不能从“没有性关系”推出，更不能仅仅由“爱情会限制主体的选择”推出。因为问题恰恰在于，为什么爱情必须关闭的那些选择中，性行为具有一种不可替代的特权地位。因此，这场争论真正的理论分界并不是“一个人是否应该拥有多个伴侣”，也不是“欲望是否应该得到满足”，而是爱的唯一性究竟属于哪一个层次。如果所谓唯一只是指被爱者在主体的爱情、人生承诺与不可替代性中占据一个无法被其他人比较的位置，那么允许其他情色关系并不构成直接矛盾；如果齐泽克要进一步主张，这种不可替代性只有通过对所有其他性对象的现实排除才能存在，那么他必须为这一更强的命题提供独立理由。本文因此并未证明齐泽克是错误的。相反，齐泽克已经提供了我们不能忽略的最强反驳：开放关系可能把爱重新降低为需求管理，可能把他人功能化，也可能通过不断保留选择而拒绝真正的承诺。本文所指出的只是，这些危险都还不足以构成一个概念上的不可能性证明。它们说明非独占关系可以失败于激进之爱，却没有证明非独占关系必然失败于激进之爱。于是，整个问题最终可以被收缩到一个比“单偶还是非单偶”更基本的问题：如果真正的爱要求主体把某一个偶然的人确立为不可替代的“唯一者”，那么这种唯一性为什么必须进一步扩展为对于主体全部情色实践的垄断权？ 将全文压缩为一个最终推论，齐泽克已经有力地建立了 RadicalLove(A)\Rightarrow Singular(A) 以及 RadicalLove(A)\Rightarrow Reorganize(\Omega), 但要进一步得到 RadicalLove(A) \Rightarrow  orall B
eq A,\ 
eg Act(E(B)), 仍然需要桥接前提 Act(E(B))\Rightarrow
eg Singular(A). 而本文所争论的，恰恰就是最后这个前提。齐泽克已经充分解释了为什么爱必须产生某种切断（cut）；他尚未充分解释的，是为什么这条切断必须恰好画在这里。

title: Reading Response
text: 1 Reading Response for Feb 5In your response, consider the ways you are positioned by systems of settler colonialism. Use a quote from the Tuck & Yang reading to help you to explore this positioning (at least 250 words)Decolonization, which we assert is a distinct project from other civil and human rights-based social justice projects, is far too often subsumed into the directives of these projects, with no regard for how decolonization wants something different than those forms of justice. Settler scholars swap out prior civil and human rights based terms, seemingly to signal both an awareness of the significance of Indigenous and decolonizing theorizations of schooling and educational research, and to include Indigenous peoples on the list of considerations as an additional special (ethnic) group or class.如果你用这篇论文的逻辑去审视女权主义，得出的结论会非常震撼： “去父权化”不是一个关于“爱与理解”的比喻，它是一场权力的移交。 那些试图通过“教育男性”或“缓慢改善”来达到目的的女权主义，在作者眼中可能只是一种“走向清白的举动”，其结果是掩盖了父权制作为一个持续运行的压迫结构的事实。1.1 关于男性的“无辜感”：结构性原罪这正是你提到的那个最核心的点。根据论文逻辑，一个男性强调自己“主观无辜”是没有意义的：位置即参与：作者认为定居者即使生下来是无辜的，但只要他占据着被窃取的土地，他就在参与殖民。同理，男性生在一个父权社会，即便他主观上从未羞辱过任何女性，但他依然在结构上受益于男性特权拒绝“无辜的举动”：如果一个男性说“我没压迫过女性，所以我不该被指责”，在 Tuck 和 Yang 看来，这正是一种“走向清白的举动”。这种强调是为了“拯救男性的未来”，是为了在不放弃特权的前提下，获得心理上的慰藉和道德上的豁免。如果将这篇论文的逻辑完全应用到女性主义（Feminism）上，它确实会从根本上反对绝大多数主流的、改良式的、或者说不够激进的女性主义流派。根据 Tuck 和 Yang 的理论框架，这种反对主要体现在以下几个层面：1. 反对“比喻化”：去父权化不是为了“改善”现有的系统主流女性主义往往致力于在现有社会、学校和工作场所中争取更多的平等和包容。但作者明确指出，这种将激进诉求转化为“改善社会和学校”的做法，实际上是将其变成了比喻（Metaphor） 。实质性要求：正如去殖民化意味着字面上的“归还土地” ，去父权化在这种逻辑下也应被视为一种实质性的、毁灭性的权力移交，而不仅仅是提高女性的地位。拒绝驯化：作者认为，将激进运动纳入现有的“社会正义”或“人权”框架，会使其“家庭化”和“驯化”，从而限制了它彻底改变世界秩序的潜力 。2. 识别“男性走向清白的举动” (Male Moves to Innocence)你提到的男性感到“主观无辜”的现象，在文中可以对应为“定居者走向清白的举动” 。主流女性主义有时会试图安抚男性，告诉他们“女性主义对男性也有好处”。但这篇文章的逻辑会冷峻地指出：特权与共犯：即使一个人主观上没有进行压迫行为，但他只要在这个父权制结构中受益，他就不再是“无辜的” 。逃避责任的策略：强调个人无辜其实是一种“逃避策略”，目的是在不真正放弃权力、特权或既得利益的前提下，减轻自己的罪恶感 。这被作者称为“拯救定居者（或男性）的未来” 。3. “不可调和的伦理” (An Ethic of Incommensurability)主流女性主义通常寻求一种“双赢”或“共识”。但 Tuck 和 Yang 强调的是“不可调和性” 。拒绝妥协：作者认为，真正的变革不是一个“折中”或“妥协”的过程，而是一个“彻底混乱的计划”，旨在改变世界的秩序 。不安的团结：真正的团结不应该是消除分歧，而是承认目标之间的冲突。这种团结是“不安的、有所保留的、未解决的” 。对于很多主流流派追求的“和谐平等”，这套逻辑会认为那是对现状的掩盖。4. 目标是“别处” (An Elsewhere)，而非“并列” (An And)主流女性主义往往是在现有国家和法律框架内的“附加项”。但作者强调：主权vs.权利：去殖民化追求的是主权，而不是在定居者国家内的公民权或人权 。彻底的断裂：去父权化在这种逻辑下，不应该只是在现有社会里加一个“性别平等”的选项，而是要走向一个不再受父权逻辑支配的“别处” 。所以如果运用 Tuck 和 Yang 的逻辑，那些主张“通过温和教育改变男性想法”、“通过职业晋升实现女性赋权”或者“在现有法律框架内追求平权”的女性主义，都会被视为在玩弄“比喻”，是在试图“拯救父权制的未来”而非彻底终结它。这种逻辑确实会导致合作变得“非常不友好” 。正如作者所言，这种关注“不会让任何人从去殖民化（或去父权化）那艰巨、令人不安的工作中解脱出来” 。它追求的是一种“危险的、清晰的”思考方式，即使这种方式会推翻我们对“社会进步”的几乎所有主流理解 。As someone who was born and raised in China, my presence in the United States places me in a complicated structural position that Tuck and Yang describe as being invited to be a settler. Even though my personal history is rooted in a land that has its own ancient sovereignty, I am positioned as a brown settler because my pursuit of education, career, and a home here is built upon a foundation of stolen Indigenous land.In this set of settler colonial relations, colonial subjects who are displaced by external colonialism, as well as racialized and minoritized by internal colonialism, still occupy and settle stolen Indigenous land.From my perspective, this means that while some of us may experience the glass ceilings or the forever foreign status often assigned to Asian minorities in the West, the struggle for equity is still fundamentally an investment in settler colonialism if it only seeks a share of settler-appropriated wealth. This is where we are forced to recognize an ethic of incommensurability: our desire for a stable and successful future in this country is built on a homesteading worldview that requires the ongoing erasure of the Indigenous people who have creation stories (and not colonization stories) for the places where I now reside. In this context, receiving education at a university here is not a neutral act; it is a participation in a structure that insists on settler sovereignty over all things.

title: 1. 结论 notes
text: 1.1 基于当前代码结构和已有数据，我会把论文主线定为： \boxed{\text{Shared LinUCB for setup}+\text{Optimistic Recursive LSTDQ for solve}} 但要准确表述为：LSTDQ 是目前最有希望的 solve controller，而不是已经证明的端到端冠军。我不建议为了让公式看起来更对称，把 setup 的 LinUCB 换成 RLS-sandwich-LCB；也不建议当前就把 solve 主线换成 LSVI-UCB。1.2 数据真正证明了什么60³、4K 正式实验中：Solve 方法Native solveControllerEnd-to-endFixed w=1.6176.33 ms0304.81 msPPO178.45 ms7.88 ms317.25 msRecursive MC-LCB173.85 ms11.01 ms309.92 msRecursive LSTDQ-LCB161.58 ms15.51 ms307.52 msLSTDQ 相对 fixed 的 native solve 提升为 8.37\%，95% CI 为 [7.53\%,9.18\%]，这是目前最强、最可信的 solve-side 信号。但 controller overhead 吃掉了收益，因此端到端仍比 fixed 慢 0.89\%。完整数据在正式 60³/4K 记录。另外还有两个限制：各方法的 LinUCB 独立更新，LSTDQ 与 fixed 在 4000 个 case 中只有 26 个 exact same-setup matches，最后 500 个为零。因此 8.37% 是“联合系统轨迹”的优势，尚不是纯 solve-controller 因果效应。same-setup audit在固定 setup 的 500-case post-fit 诊断里，LSTDQ native total 为 272.43 ms，fixed 为 270.42 ms，没有表现出明确优势。controlled result所以现在最准确的判断是： \boxed{\text{LSTDQ 已证明会学到更快的在线 solve 轨迹，但尚未证明它是纯控制器和端到端上的最终赢家。}} 1.3 为什么 LSTDQ 特别适合当前 BoomerAMG你的状态已经包含 cycle position、residual gap、recent contraction、last cycle time、last weight、PDE coefficients 和 setup parameters，状态编码器 (line 204)因此不同 cycle 的 dynamics 可以通过状态区分，不一定需要 50 套完全独立的 Q_h。Recursive LSTDQ 则让所有 cycle 共同学习一个 288 维 value model，并通过 eligibility trace 快速传播 terminal/recovery cost。当前 LSTDQ 实现 (line 548)这与 BoomerAMG 的结构很契合：episode 长度可变；后期 cycle 样本稀少；residual dynamics 跨 cycle 有大量可共享结构；要求每个 instance 都在线更新；controller wall time必须计入目标。而现有 LSVI 将预算分给 50 个独立 stage。旧 2K checkpoint 中，前十个 stage 各约 2007 个样本，stage 20 只有 1160，stage 30 只有 122，最后几个 stage 只有 7 个左右，却仍分别拟合 160 维模型。现有实验中 LSVI native solve 为 51.61 ms、E2E 为 108.71 ms，都弱于当时的 LSTDQ；虽然协议较旧，不能当成最终裁决，但它揭示了真实的 stage sparsity 问题。LSVI 对照结果经典 LSVI-UCB 的理论吸引力来自有限时域 linear MDP 假设和 elliptical bonus；但“Q 可以近似线性”并不意味着 BoomerAMG transition kernel 满足 linear-MDP 假设。LSVI-UCB 原论文1.4 Setup bandit 不应为了对称而换掉现在的 setup LinUCB 已经是 recursive least squares mean estimator；所谓 RLS-sandwich-LCB 并不会改变 mean model，只会把 uncertainty 从 \sqrt{\phi^\top V^{-1}\phi} 换成 \sqrt{\phi^\top V^{-1}MV^{-T}\phi}. 当前 LinUCB 借助共享 context-action features，在 288 万个 mixed BoomerAMG configurations 之间泛化；编码包含数值平方、pairwise interaction、categorical one-hot 和 mixed interactions。action encoder (line 239) LinUCB scoring (line 374)而 setup residual 会同时混合：solve controller 持续学习造成的 target drift；hierarchy/model misspecification；failure/fallback shock；runtime noise。把这些再写进 sandwich covariance，可能复制 LSTDQ 曾经出现的污染问题，却没有明确收益。现有 LinUCB 已把 default end-to-end 从 388.85 ms 降到约 307 ms，因此应当保留为主方法。论文中只需说两边对齐的是决策原则，而不是 covariance 公式： \begin{aligned} \text{Setup: }&\arg\min_a\bigl(\hat c(x,a)-\alpha u_{\rm setup}(x,a)\bigr),\\ \text{Solve: }&\arg\min_a\bigl(\hat Q_c(s,a)-\beta u_{\rm solve}(s,a)\bigr). \end{aligned} 这就是统一的 optimistic cost minimization。1.5 哪些方法可能超过当前 LSTDQ我的机制性排序是：改进 confidence 和 overhead 的共享 Recursive LSTDQ最可能超过当前结果。特别值得比较 current post-fit sandwich、UCLS-derived confidence、单独 coverage matrix，以及无 confidence bonus。UCLS 已经研究过 LSTD action-value 的 context-dependent confidence，并明确指出在线控制中 TD-error proxy 可能过于保守、early errors 会影响 covariance，因此你的论文不能把 “LSTD + confidence” 本身当作新算法。UCLS 原论文共享参数的 fitted-Q / structured model-based controller这是长期最有可能真正超过 LSTDQ的新路线：显式学习 (\text{residual state},w)\rightarrow (\text{next contraction},\text{cycle time}) 再规划 time-to-tolerance。它利用了 solver dynamics 的物理结构，可能更可解释、sample-efficient，也可能更低开销。但目前没有本地证据。重新校准后的 LSVI-UCB它可以成为强 baseline，但在相同 4K online budget 下，我认为超过共享 LSTDQ 的概率较低。要公平重跑，至少要修正 60³ 的 value scale、使用当前 recovery protocol，并处理 stage sparsity。它更可能在大量 offline data 或更强 cycle-position nonstationarity 下获胜。重新训练的 PPOPPO 可能在 frozen deployment 的 native solve 上超过 LSTDQ，但需要在当前 60³、当前 setup distribution 和 [1,3] action range 上重训。那回答的是“有离线训练预算时谁最好”，而不是“learn-as-you-solve 谁最好”。Recursive MC-LCB在短 online budget 下最不看好。完整 return 的方差高、credit assignment 慢，当前数据也只带来很小的 native gain。1.6 最有论文价值的故事不要把论文写成：We invented LSTDQ-LCB.LSTDQ 是经典方法，LSPI/LSTDQ 原论文；LSTD confidence exploration 也已有 UCLS。更强的贡献叙事是：A phase-aware, fully online BoomerAMG control system uses shared LinUCB to navigate a mixed combinatorial hierarchy space and recursive LSTDQ to learn state-dependent multicycle relaxation policies, while accounting for failures, recovery, learning overhead, and end-to-end wall time.这相对 Learning to Relax 的一维 SOR 参数 bandit，问题结构明显更丰富：你既选择 multilevel hierarchy，又进行 cycle-level sequential control。Learning to Relax现在最关键的五个实验是：固定同一批 (instance, setup)，比较 best fixed sweep、open-loop cycle schedule、frozen greedy LSTDQ 和正确缩放的 LSVI。加 cycle-only schedule baseline，证明 LSTDQ 的收益来自 residual/state feedback，而不只是学到了一个固定的 w_1,w_2,\ldots schedule。用当前已优化的 LSTDQ hot path重跑正式计时；现有 4K 数字尚未衡量最新精确优化。比较 no bonus、post-fit sandwich、UCLS/coverage-style confidence，并报告 calibration 与 failure rate。至少 3–5 seeds，加 held-out matrix families 和多个 grid sizes，同时分别报告 online cumulative cost 与 frozen deployment performance。如果这些实验以后 LSTDQ仍然胜出，那么结论会很强：不是“LSTDQ碰巧跑得快”，而是： \boxed{\text{在有限在线预算下，跨 cycle 共享的递归价值学习，比 stage-wise value iteration 更适合 BoomerAMG。}} 扫描结果已经出现一个很重要的事实：相对于 HYPRE 的 default setup + default solve，learned setup 通常把 setup 时间砍掉 55%–65%，但代价是产生更便宜、较弱的 hierarchy，所以 solve 部分反而比 default solve 慢。也就是说，最优秀的 joint 结果不是“setup 和 solve 都分别更快”，而是 setup 的巨大节省超过了 solve 的增加；LSTDQ 的价值是把这部分 solve penalty 尽量追回来。现在我在区分 canonical recovery-v2、已被替代的 recovery-v1，以及短窗口峰值。LSTDQ 不只是优化一个固定 hierarchy 上的 relaxation；它能够与 setup bandit共同适应，在廉价但多样的 BoomerAMG hierarchies 上学习不同的动态 relaxation strategy。Setup：84.069 → 34.916 ms，快 58.47%Native solve：36.291 → 57.003 ms，反而慢 57.07%Bandit overhead：7.099 ms最终仍净省 21.343 ms/case因此优化 bandit 的目标很明确：保持便宜的 setup，同时选择收敛质量更好的 hierarchy，降低那部分 +20.712 ms 的 solve 退化。这个实验同时表明，default setup组建了非常好的hierarchy，本身收敛很快。这意味着cycle数量少，于是LSTDQ 的学习收益不足以摊平控制开销；但是，因为LinUCB 产生了更动态、部分更难的 setup，有更多的cycle数量，LSTDQ 的逐 cycle adaptation 价值更大。对，你看得很准。不过更准确的描述不是“从第 10 个 cycle 开始一直使用高 w”，而是：两个 learner 都学出了一个接近第 9 个 AMG cycle 的强 over-relaxation 脉冲，随后根据状态在高、低 w 之间切换。图里的纵坐标从 0 开始，所以亮带出现在 y\approx8，实际对应第 9 个 cycle。在最后 1000 个、策略基本稳定的 instances 中：LinUCB v4：第 9 cycle 有 87.5% 使用 w\ge2.75，主要是 w=2.8，并不是通常用 3.0。LinUCB v5：第 9 cycle 有 89.5% 使用 w\ge2.75，其中 88.7% 直接使用 w=3.0。两者在同一个 instance 上同时选择高 w 的比例达到 79.6%。所以这条亮黄色横带确实是非常稳定的共同策略，不只是视觉巧合。但第 10 cycle 之后并非持续高 w。例如第 10 cycle：v4：约 39.7% 选择高 w，47.3% 选择低 w\le1.25。v5：约 40.9% 选择高 w，52.1% 选择低 w\le1.25。也就是说，策略更像： \text{前期中等 }w \;\rightarrow\; \text{第9 cycle 强力 }w \;\rightarrow\; \text{根据 residual 状态进行高/低修正} 这有点像一种“脉冲式 over-relaxation”或近似 bang-bang controller。尤其有意思的是，v4 和 v5 的 setup context 不同，但 solve learner 仍然发现了相同的宏观结构，说明第 9 cycle 附近进行一次激进修正很可能是这个 PDE/solver 组合本身的稳定特征。不过两者也有区别：v4 后面仍然更频繁地在 1.2 和 2.8 两端摆动；v5 在脉冲之后逐渐更多采用 w\approx2.05 的中间值。这可能与 v5 后期 cycle 更少、速度更快有关，但目前只能说相关，还不能证明因果。另外，第 9 cycle 时这批 instance 基本都还没有结束，所以这条亮带并不是“只有难题活到后面”造成的 survivor bias——它确实是一个很强的学习结果。

title: 2. 之前的Proof
text: –The regret and payback guarantees apply to contextual setup tuning under a fixed downstream solve policy. The fully joint setup–solve learner is evaluated empirically because the evolving solve policy induces a nonstationary setup-cost function.–Below, we establish two complementary guarantees: a finite-time cumulative wall-clock guarantee for contextual setup tuning, and a structural characterization of when per-cycle adaptation can outperform any fixed relaxation policy.1. Payback corollary论文叙事价值最高；1.2 Wall-clock regret theorem保证 payback 有数学基础；（Recursive LSTDQ equivalence lemma：实现正确性保障。）1.3 nonstationary relaxation theorem1.3.1 能不能证明 nonstationary 必定比 best fixed 好？不能。这个命题本身是假的。如果某个固定 w^* 已经在所有相关误差模态上最优，那么切换权重只会相同或更差。理论上只能证明两件事。1.3.1.1 第一：最佳 nonstationary policy 不会比最佳 fixed policy 差因为 fixed policy 是 nonstationary policy class 的特例：\Pi_{\mathrm{fixed}} \subseteq \Pi_{\mathrm{nonstat}} so\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{nonstat}}}T(\pi) \le \inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{fixed}}}T(\pi)这是必然成立的，但只是“不会更差”，不是严格更好。1.3.1.2 第二：在明确条件下严格更好只有当存在某个序列\sigma，满足 \Gamma_\sigma>\Gamma_{\mathrm{fix}} 时，才能证明严格优势。直观上，它要求不同权重具有互补作用：高 w 擅长压制一类误差模态；低 w 擅长压制另一类模态；两步乘积同时压制两类模态；任何单一 w 都无法兼顾。在共同特征向量的简化情形： E(w)v_j=\lambda_j(w)v_j, high–low 严格优于 fixed 的充分条件可以写成： \frac{ -\log\max_j |\lambda_j(w_H)\lambda_j(w_L)| }{ \tau(w_H)+\tau(w_L) } > \sup_w \frac{ -\log\max_j|\lambda_j(w)| }{ \tau(w) }这才是理论上可证明的 strict improvement condition。1.3.2 证明固定 hierarchy H ，令一次 AMG cycle 的误差传播算子为： E_H(w), 时间为 \tau_H(w) 。 最佳 fixed relaxation 的渐近单位时间收缩率为： \Gamma_{\mathrm{fix}}=\sup _w \frac{-\log \rho\left(E_H(w)\right)}{\tau_H(w)} . 对任意周期序列 \sigma=\left(w_1, \ldots, w_p\right), 定义： \begin{gathered} P_\sigma=E_H\left(w_p\right) \cdots E_H\left(w_1\right), \\ \Gamma_\sigma=\frac{-\log \rho\left(P_\sigma\right)}{\sum_{i=1}^p \tau_H\left(w_i\right)} . \end{gathered} 如果： \Gamma_\sigma>\Gamma_{\mathrm{fix}}, 那么对充分严格的 tolerance，重复该非平稳周期在 wall－clock time 上严格优于所有 fixed w 。你的 high－low pattern 对应： \sigma=\left(w_H, w_L\right) . 1.3.3

title: 3. Dynamic RL activation and a defensible theoretical framework
text:
Working theory note, 2026-09-12. This is a proposed analysis, not a claim that the current joint implementation satisfies every assumption below. No new PDE experiments were run for this note.1. Experimental contract and evidenceThe current main configuration uses scalar anisotropic diffusion, Canonical 8D setup context, LinUCB-v5 with structured candidate sets, and Recursive LSTDQ-v3. The corrected 60³ experiment has 5,000 problems in the total budget, with fixed-weight solve for the first 1,000 and joint learning thereafter. Setup continues learning after solve control begins. The solve configuration is weighted ℓ₁-Jacobi on the down/up sweeps, direct coarse solve (18/18/9), relative tolerance 10⁻⁶, and a 50-cycle cap. The action grid is 1, 1.05, …, 3.The corrected state encoder distinguishes the actual setup categories and maps the previous weight over its actual range. The solve representation has 35 state features and 9 action-basis features, hence 315 joint features. Its update uses the executed next action, discount 1, and trace parameter 0.8: it is a SARSA-type recursive LSTDQ(λ) control scheme.In the latest corrected five-method run, Canonical + LSTDQ averaged 209.502 ms native time versus 372.856 ms for the baseline, a 43.81% reduction. Including the reported learner/controller overhead gives 221.270 ms, a 40.66% reduction. These are different cost definitions. The native reduction agrees with the corrected three-seed range, 43.55%–44.52%; that agreement does not isolate a causal effect of the encoder repair, since timing conditions and resulting learning paths differed across runs.The previous prefix audit covered 11 experiment directories and 43 learning trajectories. These are descriptive trajectories, not 43 independent replications. In the latest Canonical staged branch, first-attempt failures in cases 1–100, 101–200, 201–400, 401–600, 601–800, and 801–1000 were respectively 76%, 39%, 5.5%, 1%, 1%, and 1.5%. All 133 prefix failures were solve nonconvergence. The full 5,000-problem run had 142 primary failures, all recovered.The audit found occasional rebounds and materially more persistent failure in advection experiments. A permanent sharp change is therefore a useful model to analyze, not an established property of all trajectories.Sources: latest report, prefix audit, corrected seed report, experiment configuration.2. What the activation problem actually estimatesFor problem t, during the setup-only phase, defineY_t=\mathbf 1\{	ext{the first primary attempt does not reach the prescribed tolerance within its budget}\}.Count failure before retry/fallback, once per problem. A recovered failure remains Y_t=1. For a general deployment, inability to construct the primary hierarchy also counts as primary unreliability; alternatively, it can be reported as a separate event while remaining in the gate’s denominator.Let \mathcal F_{t-1} contain the observed learning history before the next problem is revealed, and definep_t=\mathbb E[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}].This is the conditional failure risk of the deployed setup-selection procedure paired with the fixed solve policy. It averages over the next problem and any relevant algorithmic randomness. It is not the failure probability for every individual PDE context or every candidate action. The probability model is over problem streams/randomness; conditioning on a completely fixed deterministic benchmark and all its random seeds would not yield an empirical Bernoulli sampling model.The relevant scientific question is whether primary reliability has improved enough to enable solve-policy learning. It is not whether setup parameters, predictions, or the setup optimizer have converged.There is no distribution-free implication from an arbitrarily long successful history to low next-step risk: two processes can have identical observations through time t and different next-step failure probabilities. In particular, one can change to certain failure immediately after a data-dependent activation time. Thus a stopping rule needs an explicit target and an explicit statement of what its error control means.A fixed window is not inherently mathematically invalid. The difficulty with the current rule is its heuristic calibration and the gap between a historical rate and current/future risk. Repeatedly checking ordinary 95% binomial intervals does not supply simultaneous 95% coverage. CUSUM average-run-length control is also different from controlling the probability of any false activation.3. Recommended criterion: a mixture sequential testChoose, before inspecting the evaluation trajectories:p_{m bad}\in(0,1): an operationally unacceptable primary-failure rate;p_{m good}\in(0,p_{m bad}): a design rate at which timely detection is desired;\delta\in(0,1): the allowed probability of a false activation under persistent unreliability.The gap between the two rates is an indifference region, not a claim that risk makes a discontinuous jump. For illustration only, one might use p_{m bad}=0.05, p_{m good}=0.01, and \delta=0.05. These numbers are not calibrated recommendations for this experiment.Define the one-step evidence factor\ell_t= \left( rac{p_{m good}}{p_{m bad}}ight)^{Y_t} \left( rac{1-p_{m good}}{1-p_{m bad}}ight)^{1-Y_t}. 	ag{1}For each possible onset k, letL_{k,t}=  egin{cases} 1,&t<k,\ \prod_{i=k}^{t}\ell_i,&t\ge k. \end{cases}Choose deterministic weights \omega_k>0 with \sum_{k\ge1}\omega_k=1. A simple horizon-free choice is\omega_k= rac1{k(k+1)}.Combine all onsets, retaining the mass assigned to as-yet-unstarted tests:M_t=\sum_{k=1}^{t}\omega_kL_{k,t}+\sum_{k>t}\omega_k, \qquad M_0=1. 	ag{2}The activation boundary and first RL-controlled problem are	au=\inf\{t\ge1:M_t\ge1/\delta\}, \qquad 	ext{first RL problem}=	au+1. 	ag{3}If the set is empty within the stream, solve remains fixed for that stream. Any imposed deadline that activates RL without crossing (3) is a separate protocol decision outside this certificate.The statistic tests every problem and accounts for every possible onset. Early failures penalize tests that started early, but do not contaminate all subsequently started tests. There is no fixed observation window or arbitrary number of passing blocks.For the displayed weights, implementation needs only a scalar accumulator:B_0=0,\qquad B_t=\ell_t\left(B_{t-1}+ rac1{t(t+1)}ight), \qquad M_t=B_t+ rac1{t+1}. 	ag{4}Thus time and storage per problem are O(1). Compute in log space for numerical stability. This is an algebraic recursion, not an implemented change to the runner.For a known maximum horizon T, \omega_k=1/T, k=1,…,T, is an alternative with a simpler onset penalty \log T. The horizon must be chosen prospectively; extending it after observing evidence requires a new valid allocation. Other predetermined proper weights preserve validity and change detection delay. The weights represent an explicit cost of searching over unknown onset times, not an unacknowledged window length.3.3.1 Proposition 1: control of false activationSuppose p_t\ge p_{m bad} almost surely at every monitored time. Then\Pr(	au<\infty)\le\delta. 	ag{5}More locally, if the inequality holds for t<ν, with deterministic ν, then\Pr(	au<

Conditional on \mathcal F_{t-1},\mathbb E[\ell_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}] =p_t rac{p_{m good}}{p_{m bad}} +(1-p_t) rac{1-p_{m good}}{1-p_{m bad}} \le1.The expression is decreasing in p_t and equals one at p_t=p_{m bad}. Each L_{k,t} is consequently a nonnegative supermartingale starting at one under the null. Their proper mixture is also one. Ville’s inequality gives (5). See Howard et al., time-uniform Chernoff bounds and Howard et al., confidence sequences. At 1% actual failure risk the expected increment is about 0.02474. Occasional failures are therefore allowed, but a sustained low-risk run is needed. A stringent certificate need not activate earlier than 1,000 on every trajectory.3.3.3 Precisely what is, and is not, certifiedWithout an assumption relating past and future risk, crossing (3) rejects the persistent-unreliability hypothesis. It does not itself prove p_{	au+1}\le p_{m bad}, and certainly does not prove that the newly activated RL controller has that risk.Under a permanent two-regime model, (9) has the useful interpretation that activation occurs after the reliable regime begins, with controlled early-activation probability and finite detection delay. A gradual decline with an interval between the two thresholds can be handled by distinguishing the end of the certified bad regime from the start of the good regime. No delay guarantee is promised while risk remains inside the indifference region.The actual setup policy continues exploring and can experience rebounds. Thus the paper should call this a sequential reliability-based activation rule and state the durable-improvement assumption for its readiness interpretation. It should not label the event “setup convergence” or an unconditional safety guarantee.If a single good design rate is undesirable, mix (1) over several predetermined alternatives below p_{m bad}, with proper weights. The same proof applies. This costs a small number of scalar recursions and an additional log-weight term in the delay bound. Choosing an alternative retrospectively without a mixture or multiplicity correction is not covered.4. Stronger current-risk statements require a drift modelA complementary formulation makes the missing assumption especially visible. For every suffix [k,t], let n=t−k+1 and\widehat p_{k,t}= rac1n\sum_{i=k}^tY_i,\qquad  ar p_{k,t}= rac1n\sum_{i=k}^tp_i.Allocate \delta_{k,n}=\delta/[k(k+1)n(n+1)]. Conditional Hoeffding concentration and a union bound yield, simultaneously for all k and t, with probability at least 1−δ, ar p_{k,t}\le \widehat p_{k,t}+ \sqrt{ rac{\log(k(k+1)n(n+1)/\delta)}{2n}}. 	ag{10}If a known, valid drift envelope satisfiesp_{t+1}\le p_i+d_{i,t+1}\quad	ext{for every }i\le t,then a current-risk upper bound isU_t=\min\left\{1,\ \min_{1\le k\le t} \left[ \widehat p_{k,t} +\sqrt{ rac{\log(k(k+1)n(n+1)/\delta)}{2n}} + rac1n\sum_{i=k}^td_{i,t+1} ight]ight\}. 	ag{11}The stopping time 	au_U=\inf\{t:U_t\le p_{m tol}\} satisfies\Pr\{	au_U<\infty,\ p_{	au_U+1}>p_{m tol}\}\le\delta, 	ag{12}for the continued fixed-solve process. Formula (10) alone only concerns averages of historical conditional means; it cannot be substituted directly into (12).For nonincreasing risk one can set d=0. For a known one-step upward drift bound p_{j+1}-p_j\le v, the correction is v(n+1)/2. The minimization in (11) then selects a history length through an explicit tradeoff between sampling error and drift. Neither monotonicity nor a suitably small v follows from ordinary LinUCB updates or from a smoothed plot.This version is stronger in its target but stronger in assumptions and computational cost. The Hoeffding bound is intentionally elementary and can be conservative for rare failures. A sharper Bernoulli/martingale bound can replace it after the target and drift assumption have been settled.5. Setup regret and payback: what can be proved for which algorithmFix the downstream solve and recovery policy. Let C_t be the candidate set available before the current cost observation, let \phi_t(a)\in\mathbb R^d, and assume\mu_t(a)=\phi_t(a)^	op	heta_\star,\qquad Y_t^{m cost}=\mu_t(a_t)+\xi_t,with bounded features and parameter norm and conditionally sub-Gaussian, mean-zero noise. Use a new notation Y_t^{m cost} to distinguish cost from the binary gate observation.For V_t=\lambda I+\sum_{i=1}^t\phi_i(a_i)\phi_i(a_i)^	op, a valid simultaneous radius has the familiar form eta_t= \sigma\sqrt{2\log  rac{\det(V_t)^{1/2}}{\det(\lambda I)^{1/2}\delta}} +\sqrt{\lambda}\,\|	heta_\star\|_{m bound}. 	ag{13}An LCB policy using this radius and minimizing over C_t has candidate-set pseudo-regret \widetilde O(d\sqrt T), under the standard boundedness/scaling conditions. History-dependent candidate generation is allowed; the current noise cannot be used to define the candidate set. This is an application of existing linear-bandit theory, not a new general regret result. See Abbasi-Yadkori, Pál, and Szepesvári (2011).The implemented structured-512 path enables alpha decay, and v5 inherits v4’s coefficient \alpha_t=\alpha_0/\sqrt{t+1}, up to indexing/burn-in. It is not (13). See construction and coefficient.A useful deterministic inequality exposes the exact extra requirement. On the confidence event, put u_t(a)=\|\phi_t(a)\|_{V_{t-1}^{-1}} and a_t^\star\in\arg\min_{a\in C_t}\mu_t(a). The implemented LCB choice satisfies\mu_t(a_t)-\mu_t(a_t^\star) \le( eta_{t-1}+\alpha_t)u_t(a_t) +( eta_{t-1}-\alpha_t)_+u_t(a_t^\star). 	ag{14}Proof. Use confidence bounds on the chosen and oracle actions, with \widehat\mu_t(a_t)-\alpha_tu_t(a_t) \le\widehat\mu_t(a_t^\star)-\alpha_tu_t(a_t^\star). ∎The first sum in (14) admits the usual elliptical-potential control. The second is a coverage deficit and is not automatically sublinear. One possible sufficient condition is \lambda_{\min}(V_t|_{\mathcal S})\ge\kappa t eventually on the identifiable feature span \mathcal S; it gives u_t(a_t^\star)=O(t^{-1/2}). This is a substantial persistent-excitation assumption, not a consequence of sampling 512 candidate actions. Only executed actions enter V. Using the feature span matters because Canonical 8D contains a redundant common-scale feature.Forced initial-guess rounds must be accounted for separately; a fixed number contributes only a bounded additive term when per-round regret is bounded.Thus there are two honest routes: analyze a confidence-calibrated variant, or retain the existing algorithm and supply assumptions controlling the second term in (14). Do not silently identify the current decay rule with the textbook confidence policy.The theorem also needs an exact cost contract. If the regression target includes recovery or controller time, the oracle must use the same quantity. Correlated suffix-cost labels from several recovery decisions do not automatically form one unbiased bandit observation per problem. Warmup is included in the total problem budget.Full-action-space regret additionally contains \sum_t[\min_{a\in C_t}\mu_t(a)-\min_{a\in\mathcal A}\mu_t(a)]. Candidate-set regret alone does not control it.Once RL changes the downstream solve policy, setup costs become policy-dependent. Fixed-downstream realizability does not establish stationary realizability for the joint run. The gate does not remove this issue. A joint guarantee would need a drift/tracking term, a suitable changing-parameter model, or a separately justified restriction.For payback, define the candidate oracle’s cumulative advantage G_T, the learner’s candidate regret R_T, and overhead H_T, without counting the same cost twice. The expected/pseudo accounting identity is\operatorname{Savings}(T)=G_T-R_T-H_T.If G_T\ge gT-B_G, H_T\le hT+B_H, g>h, and R_T=o(T), eventual positive savings follows. For a quantitative payback bound, solve (g-h)T>R_T+B_G+B_H. Positive average oracle advantage by itself is insufficient when overhead consumes it. An assertion about realized savings holding for every sufficiently large T additionally requires a uniform stochastic bound or an appropriate strong law. This is naturally a corollary.6. Nonstationary relaxation: repair and strengthen the solver resultFor a fixed nonsingular system A and fixed hierarchy, write error propagation as e^+=E_H(w)e. Residual propagation is r^+=AE_H(w)A^{-1}r; the spectral radius is unchanged, while finite-tolerance norm behavior need not be.The proposed spectral-rate inequality does not imply that the periodic policy beats every fixed weight for every initial residual. For example, with equal cycle costs,E_L=\operatorname{diag}(0.9,0.1),\qquad E_H=\operatorname{diag}(0.1,0.9),the periodic product is 0.09I, with better worst-case asymptotic rate than either fixed action. But on e_0=(0,1)^	op, fixed L contracts by 0.1 per step and is asymptotically faster than the periodic policy’s 0.3 per-step rate.3.6.1 Proposition 3: a correct worst-case asymptotic comparisonLet the action set be finite, as in the implemented 41-weight grid. Assume fixed positive per-cycle costs, fixed linear operators, and 0<ho(E_H(w))<1 for the fixed-action comparators. For a period σ let P_\sigma=E_H(w_p)\cdots E_H(w_1), c_\sigma=\sum_i	au_H(w_i), and 0<ho(P_\sigma)<1.Define fixed-policy time by the first iterate whose induced residual-propagation norm is at most ε, and define periodic time using period-end iterates. Then\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}  rac{T_w^{m wc}(\epsilon)}{\log(1/\epsilon)} = rac{	au_H(w)}{-\logho(E_H(w))},\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}  rac{T_\sigma^{m wc}(\epsilon)}{\log(1/\epsilon)} = rac{c_\sigma}{-\logho(P_\sigma)}. 	ag{15}Consequently a strict gap in the proposed spectral contraction per unit cost yields a uniform small-tolerance advantage over the finite set of fixed comparators, in this worst-case sense.Proof sketch. For a stable matrix B, ho(B)^n\le\|B^n\|, while for each r>ho(B) there is a constant C_r with \|B^n\|\le C_rr^n. These give matching leading hitting-time bounds as ε→0 and r↓ρ(B). Similarity by fixed A changes the norm constants but not the leading rate. A finite comparator set permits one common sufficiently small tolerance. Stopping inside a period can only improve the periodic method’s time. ∎A continuum of comparators requires a corresponding uniform argument. Unstable fixed comparators cannot meet arbitrarily strict worst-case tolerances. Nilpotent/zero-radius operators require a separate finite-termination statement. Actual finite-tolerance performance also depends on transient amplification, starting residuals, failure caps, and timing variability.3.6.2 Constructive witness inside an idealized two-grid modelThere is a more informative result than merely assuming that a superior product exists. ConsiderA= egin{pmatrix}2/3&-1/3\-1/3&2/3\end{pmatrix}, \qquad D_{\ell_1}=I, \qquad P= rac12 egin{pmatrix}\sqrt3-1\\sqrt3+1\end{pmatrix}.Use one weighted ℓ₁-Jacobi pre-sweep and one identical post-sweep, S(w)=I-wA, with exact Galerkin coarse correction C=I-P(P^	op AP)^{-1}P^	op A. The two-grid error operator is E(w)=S(w)CS(w).In A-energy coordinates and the eigenbasis of A, C becomes the projection onto u=(1,1)^	op/\sqrt2, so\widetilde E(w)=v(w)v(w)^	op,\qquad v(w)= rac1{\sqrt2}(1-w/3,\ 1-w)^	op.Hence, over all w\in[1,3],\min_who(E(w)) =\min_w rac{(1-w/3)^2+(1-w)^2}{2} = rac15, \quad w_{m best}= rac65. 	ag{16}For w_L=1 and w_H=2.9=29/10, both on the experimental action grid,v(w_H)^	op v(w_L)= rac1{90},\qquad ho(E(w_H)E(w_L))= rac1{8100}. 	ag{17}With equal per-cycle costs, the periodic effective spectral factor is therefore 1/90<1/5, strictly better than every fixed weight. Meanwhile ho(E(2.9))=65/36>1: the high-weight cycle alone is unstable. The strict gap is robust to sufficiently small perturbations of this finite-dimensional model. The limiting pair 1 and 3 even has a zero two-cycle product, but the nonzero-radius example (17) avoids relying on exact annihilation.Each fixed operator in this example is self-adjoint in energy coordinates, giving the uniform bound \|E(w)^n\|_A\ge5^{-n}. If F=E(2.9)E(1), its rank-one form gives F^n=ho(F)^{n-1}F. These two identities directly supply the eventual norm-based time advantage, including uniformity over the continuum of fixed weights.This is an existence theorem for a precisely specified two-grid model sharing weighted ℓ₁-Jacobi and exact coarse correction. It does not assert that the observed 60³ BoomerAMG hierarchies realize these matrices or that a particular high–low pair is optimal there.Nonstationary relaxation has a substantial existing numerical-analysis literature. The manuscript should distinguish this solver mechanism from any novelty of learning a hierarchy- and residual-dependent feedback policy. Relevant primary sources include Adsuara et al., scheduled relaxation and Richardson and Lottes, optimal polynomial smoothers for multigrid V-cycles. Whole AMG-cycle operators are not automatically polynomials in a single matrix.7. What the LSTDQ statements can establish3.7.1 RepresentabilityWriting Q_	heta(s,w)=b(w)^	op\Theta x(s) shows state–action interactions. A pairwise preference reversal is expressible when the relevant action-basis rows and history features distinguish the two cases. Merely listing last-weight and residual features is not a proof that arbitrary policies or true value functions are representable.For the actual normalized compact-RBF basis, a concrete endpoint construction is available. Let b_1,b_9 denote the basis components centered at weights 1 and 3, and set g(w)=b_9(w)-b_1(w). On the current grid, g has its unique minimum at 1 and maximum at 3. The endpoint basis components have disjoint support; normalization makes each attain its unique maximum at its own endpoint. With the encoded previous weight z=(w_{m last}-2), the class containsQ(s,w)=c+z\,g(w).Minimizing Q chooses 3 after previous weight 1 and chooses 1 after previous weight 3. The constant c can make all values nonnegative. This proves expressibility of a nonconstant alternating policy over the full grid, not that training finds it or that it is optimal.The same action-scoring class could also be used by a history-augmented contextual bandit. Sequential credit assignment comes from action-dependent solver dynamics and the multi-step cost target, not from representability alone.3.7.2 Conditional preservation of a fixed-policy advantageUse a finite horizon K, including an absorbing terminal state and a consistently defined failure/recovery terminal cost. Let Q_h^{\pi^\star} be cost-to-go for a reference policy, and suppose uniformly over relevant histories/states and actions that|\widehat Q_h-Q_h^{\pi^\star}|\le\varepsilon_Q.If \widehat\pi_h minimizes \widehat Q_h, thenJ(\widehat\pi)\le J(\pi^\star)+2K\varepsilon_Q. 	ag{18}Therefore 2K\varepsilon_Q<\Delta_{m fix} preserves strict superiority to the best fixed comparator under the same initial-state distribution and cost definition.Proof. Approximate greediness gives Q_h^{\pi^\star}(s,\widehat\pi_h(s))-V_h^{\pi^\star}(s)\le2\varepsilon_Q. The finite-horizon performance-difference identity sums these advantages along trajectories of \widehat\pi. ∎The reference need not be globally optimal. This is a generic approximate-policy-improvement proposition, not yet an LSTDQ estimation theorem. See Lagoudakis and Parr, LSPI for the broader policy-evaluation/improvement framework.The actual policy uses an uncertainty bonus, clipping, and epsilon exploration. If its conditional mean selection slack in estimated Q is at most \zeta_h, (18) becomesJ(\widehat\pi_{m deployed}) \le J(\pi^\star)+2K\varepsilon_Q+ \mathbb E\sum_{h=0}^{K-1}\zeta_h. 	ag{19}Any controller cost omitted from Q must also be added when comparing wall time. The real cycle cap can provide K; an informal effective horizon cannot replace a termination assumption.The 35-dimensional encoder has not been shown to be Markov-sufficient. Use full solver states or histories for the theorem, then state the approximation assumption for their encoded representation. Equal residual norms do not identify equal residual directions.For a prospective LSTDQ-specific bridge, the deterministic identity\widehat	heta_N-	heta_\star =A_N^{-1}\left[ \sum_{i=1}^Nz_i(c_i-v_i^	op	heta_\star) -\lambda_{m ridge}	heta_\star ight], \quad v_i=\psi_i-\gamma\psi_{i+1}, 	ag{20}separates Bellman approximation/bias, moment concentration, and conditioning of A_N. Under an appropriate fixed-policy moment model, bounded moments, and a nondegenerate normalized A_N, this provides a route to parameter and uniform Q bounds. The evolving joint behavior policy does not automatically satisfy those fixed-policy assumptions.3.7.3 Recursive equals batchFor the same committed transitions, executed next actions, terminal indicators, trace resets, discount, trace parameter, and ridge,z_i=\gamma\lambda_{m trace}z_{i-1}+\psi_i,\quad A_N=\lambda_{m ridge}I+\sum_i z_i(\psi_i-\gamma\psi_{i+1})^	op,\quad b_N=\sum_i z_ic_i.If every required prefix A_i is nonsingular and the inverse updates are valid, Sherman–Morrison gives 	heta_N^{m rec}=A_N^{-1}b_N in exact arithmetic. This is equivalence to a batch accumulation of the same historical estimating equations, not to LSPI recomputing every target under a newly chosen single policy.Positive ridge alone does not guarantee nonsingularity for this nonsymmetric estimating matrix. The implementation’s pseudoinverse safeguards and floating-point behavior need separate qualification when the nonsingularity assumption fails. See recursive mean update.3.7.4 Optional covariance analysisEpisode clustering addresses dependence within solves, but does not itself establish confidence coverage. V3 accumulates episode scores evaluated at different historical post-fit parameters. Consistency would require an appropriate parameter limit, negligible historical-parameter evaluation error, a nonsingular limiting estimating matrix, moment/Lindeberg conditions, and either cross-episode martingale orthogonality or a covariance estimator accounting for cross-episode dependence. Fixed-policy asymptotic intervals would still not be anytime-valid exploration bounds. This can remain outside the principal theorem claims.8. Suggested paper scope and genuinely necessary validationA coherent three-part theory is:Candidate-set cost learning, with payback as a corollary and an explicit distinction between the confidence-calibrated and implemented decay rules.Sequential reliability activation, with false-activation control and detection delay under a stated durable-improvement model.Constructive nonstationary solver advantage, followed by conditional preservation under sufficiently accurate action-value estimates.Representability and recursive equivalence are supporting propositions. These are conditional modules; they do not constitute an end-to-end guarantee for the adaptive joint learner merely by being placed in sequence.The immediate work can remain theoretical. Existing histories suffice to compute the proposed activation statistic and audit what it would have observed, without new PDE solves. Such a replay would describe the gate only; it would not reconstruct the changed trajectory caused by earlier RL activation. No gate replay or calibration was performed for this note.Two additional empirical checks become necessary only if the corresponding stronger claims enter the paper:“The deployed dynamic-start method improves on fixed-1000”: this requires prospective runs with the gate fixed before evaluation, since activation changes both learners’ future data.“The learned feedback policy outperforms the best fixed or predetermined periodic relaxation on these AMG systems”: this requires matched systems, hierarchies, initial residuals, stopping rules, and timing definitions. The current default-weight comparison does not establish the positive \Delta_{m fix} premise. A fixed-periodic comparator is needed for a claim about feedback’s advantage over scheduling.Neither a proof of the conditional propositions nor the constructive two-grid witness requires another broad experiment sweep. The critical next theoretical decisions are the operational risk target, the meaning of the regime assumption, the exact cost contract, and which algorithm the regret statement describes.

text: 忽然看到 Emory 的新生已经迭代到 Class of 2030，心里不由得有点发慌——原来我的四年已经走完了吗？日子从某一刻开始变得越发臃肿，只是因为自己在二十出头、还有两个月就要大学毕业的时候，本该是一个要么满眼都是“忽明忽暗的云”，要么已经小有成就的年纪。而我却时常闪过这种难以言喻的念头，觉得未来没有盼头：因为自己甚至无法去理想的地方继续学业，更别提什么所谓的成就了。

title: Instruction for Lab
text: PHYS-444W-1: Adv Undergraduate Laboratory - Spring 2026 PHYS 444W/445W/544The purpose of this course is to broaden and refine your laboratory and analytical skills, to further your mastery of several fields of physics, and to communicate your results in journal-paper-style written reports and a conference-style talk.LEARNING GOALSBroaden and refine laboratory skills: You’ll learn and practice skills such as wiring op amps, aligning lasers, calibrating a spectrometer, and using sophisticated instruments such as oscilloscopes and single-photon detectors. Broaden and refine analytical skills: You’ll practice skills such as solving differential equations, using Dirac notation, performing celestial-coordinate conversions, and curve-fitting. Explore advanced physics: Through experiment, you’ll explore advanced physics topics such as hyperfine structure, Bell inequalities, and quantum cryptography. Communicate to learn. You’ll use communication as a form of inquiry, invention, and reflection. (This language is from Emory’s continuing communication GER, but it’s true: When you prepare to communicate technical information, through writing or oral presentations, you really do learn a lot.) Communicate flexibly. You’ll communicate effectively for specified audiences in more than one mode, such as written, oral, and graphical modes. You will write lab reports for the first three of your four modules. The lab reports will be written in the style of a journal paper. The target audience is a hypothetical editor or reviewer. For the fourth module, you will give a brief (5-10 minute) presentation, similar to a talk at a physics conference.QUANTUM MECHANICS:Quantum entanglement Download Quantum entanglement: Shine violet light through a beta barium borate crystal to create pairs of entangled infrared photons, and demonstrate a violation of a Bell inequality. This apparatus was funded in part by a grant from the Reichert FoundationLinks to an external site..Quantum optics analogies Download Quantum optics analogies: Investigate the quantum eraser and quantum cryptography. For simplicity, laser beams are used instead of single photons.RESEARCH INSTRUMENTS:LabVIEW Download LabVIEW: Acquire basic proficiency in sophisticated interfacing software used in many research labs. Record the IV curve of a diode, and derive the ideal diode equation.Pulsed NMR Download Pulsed NMR: Explore the physics underlying MRI.Optical pumping Download Optical pumping: Investigate hyperfine and Zeeman interactions in rubidium.AFM Download AFM: Use an atomic force microscope to investigate the structure of a CD, DVD, and Blu-Ray disc. May the atomic force be with you. (TA: Jordan Ma)OSCILLATIONS:Water-column oscillations Download Water-column oscillations: Predict and measure the frequencies of oscillating water columns.Rotary pendulum Download Rotary pendulum: Observe natural frequency, damped oscillations, resonance response, period doubling, and chaotic attractors in the motion of a rotary pendulum.Chaos in electronics Download Chaos in electronics: Construct circuits that exhibit the Lorenz attractor and other chaotic phenomena. Prerequisite: Electronics tutorials at the beginning of the course, or knowledge of op amps from other courses.APPLIED OPTICS:Spectrometer interfaced with Arduino Download Spectrometer interfaced with Arduino: Write a Python script to control a spectrometer interfaced with an Arduino microcontroller. Wow!Wave optics Download Wave optics: Observe standing waves between a micowave transmitter and receiver, interference in a glass slide, Fresnel reflection of a polarized light cone, and the effect of quarter-wave and half-wave plates.Transient heat conduction Download Transient heat conduction: Use laser beam-bending to measure and analyze the cold front passing through a material dipped in ice water.ASTRONOMY:Galactic rotation: Construct and test the Completely Hackable Amateur Radio TelescopeLinks to an external site.!Exoplanets: Join the search for planets around other stars. This will be your third or fourth module.Course policies:You may have one lab partner or work alone. To make sure you have adequate opportunity for hands-on lab experience, we avoid groups of 3 or more. (Exceptions are made for quantum entanglement.) You and your lab partner may share data, but you write separate lab reports. On the other hand, your oral presentation may be done jointly with your partner. May 5 is the final deadline for all lab reports!Grades are determined as follows:75 points Three lab reports (25 points each)25 points Oral presentation (10 points) with slides (15 points)Please don’t hesitate to contact me if you’d like help understanding any experimental principles or procedures. That’s why I’m here.Guidelines for Writing Lab Reports (New for 2026!)The goal is to write your lab reports as if they were journal papers. The target audience is a hypothetical journal editor or reviewer who has never seen our lab or read my lab manuals. You know more than your target audience; your goal is to teach the reader something they don’t already know. Your goal is to guide the reader easily and effortlessly from the familiar (basic physics) to the unfamiliar (the theoretical and experimental details of your module). Every sentence should be part of a logical, coherent narrative. You’re telling a story, with the goal of teaching; you’re not just listing facts.How to decide what to include: You may want to think about your results, including any figures and tables. What does the reader need to be taught in advance about the theory and the procedure, in order to understand your results? (Also include anything the manual specifically asks for. If the manual skips steps in derivations, fill them in. If the manual gives complete derivations, you may skip steps, explaining the missing steps in words.)How much detail to include about the procedure: You want the reader to be able to reproduce your results, but you don’t need to include every detail. You can assume the reader knows how to use an oscilloscope, for example. You don’t need to explain how it works, or state that you plugged it in and turned it on. Please do not use the imperative (align the laser); instead, state what you did (we aligned the laser). You’re not writing a manual; do not tell the reader what to do. It is acceptable and preferable to use first person (I/we) because this clarifies what you did, as opposed to what was done by others in the past.Tenses: You may use both past and present tense, even in the same sentence (we plugged in the oscilloscope because it doesn’t do anything if it’s not plugged in), but don’t randomly switch between past and present for no reason (we turned on the laser, and we align the lenses). Please avoid the word would unless you’re 100% sure there’s no other way to say what you mean.Sections of the report: The titles of your sections can be anything you want, like chapter titles in a book. Your sections don’t have to be Introduction, Procedure, etc., although they may. The only section that almost all journal papers have is the abstract.The abstract: This is a single opening paragraph advertising your achievements, typically including specific, quantitative results. The abstract is often the only free section of a journal paper; the rest of the paper may be behind a paywall. Therefore, the abstract should function as a standalone document.Clarity: Poets want every word to mean as many things as possible; science writers want exactly the opposite. Every single sentence in your report should have only one possible interpretation.Significant digits: If you have three digits in your raw data, you should have no more than three digits in your final results. Ideally, you would use error analysis to determine the number of significant digits.Error analysis: This is a sophisticated subject. A good introduction is http://user.physics.unc.edu/~deardorf/uncertainty/UNCguide.htmlLinks to an external site., which also explains how the uncertainty determines the number of significant digits to use in the measured result. A more advanced treatment is http://www.physics.umd.edu/courses/Phys261/F06/ErrorPropagation.pdfLinks to an external site..Captions: Figure captions go below the figure. Table captions go above the table. (This is an arbitrary but nearly universal rule; check any journal.) Only the first letter of each sentence is capitalized. The first sentence in a caption is typically a fragment, as in “Figure 1. The apparatus.” Subsequent sentences, if there are any, are complete sentences.Figure axes and table headers: These should be labeled with the name or symbol of the variable. The units should be in parentheses.Equations: Even sentences containing equations should be punctuated normally. Avoid sentence fragments. The format for equations is as follows:We now will study the beloved Pythagorean theorem,Equation (1) shows…. (Notice the period in the previous line!)Comma splices: These are common in informal writing, but I avoid them in formal scientific writing.Accommodate your reader: Good scientific papers accommodate both the lazy reader and the thorough reader:The lazy reader reads only the abstract and the figure captions. All the evidence that you’ve accomplished something interesting should appear in the abstract, figures, and figure captions. The abstract should stand on its own and make sense to someone who hasn’t read the rest of the paper. Each figure with its caption should similarly make sense to someone who hasn’t read the rest of the paper. The thorough reader (possibly a lazy reader impressed by your abstract and figures) wants to read a continuous narrative from start to finish. This reader will ignore your figures and tables until the text refers to them; you should guide your reader to each figure and table whenever you want your reader to look there. Authors cannot control where figures and tables appear in journal papers, so please do not write as shown in the figure below. (Instead: as shown in Fig. 1.) Capitalization of terms: I believe the most common convention in physics journals is, i.e., Maxwell’s equations, Newton’s laws, etc. (Don’t capitalize equations, laws, etc.)Plagiarism: You are expected to write your laboratory reports on your own. Any unique phrases lifted directly from any source, including the internet, must be enclosed in quotation marks with the source clearly identified. All sources that you studied to gain understanding while preparing to write your laboratory report, including links to the internet, should be listed at the end of your report under References. If you are ever in doubt, identify the source of your material. In particular, be sure to cite the source of any graphics you download into your report.I don’t like to be bossy, but please avoid these forms of plagiarism:Please do not copy entire paragraphs from any source. In physics papers, we almost never quote exact text. Please do not do a sentence-by-sentence paraphrase of any document. I know it’s hard to come up with a unique explanation of a technical topic, but the idea is to understand it well enough to pull the sentences out of your head (or your notes). Please do not use anyone else’s data in lieu of data you’re supposed to record yourself. You may, however, cite anyone else’s data for purposes of discussion.

text: 1 Theory1.1 Static pressure balanceFigure 1 defines the geometry used in the analysis. The tube has length L and cross-sectional area A. The height of the water column inside the tube is x(t), and the equilibrium value after the tube is fixed is denoted by y. The lower end of the tube is open and lies a vertical distance d below the free surface of the reservoir. The trapped air has pressure P and volume V(x)=A(L-x).At equilibrium, the water at the bottom opening is shared by the tube and the reservoir, so the pressure P_{b} there must be the same on both sides. The pressure relation from figure 1 is: \begin{aligned} & P_b=P_a+\rho g d \\ & P_b=P_{\mathrm{eq}}+\rho g y \end{aligned} where P_a is atmospheric pressure and \rho is the density of water. Therefore, we have P_{\mathrm{eq}}=P_a+\rho g(d-y) \tag{1} which shows why the trapped air matters. The pressure above the internal water column is not generally equal to atmospheric pressure.%Figure 1. should be here, no need to change anything. keep it as it is.% ## Equation of motionAfter the tube has been reclamped, d is fixed and the water column can oscillate about y. The pressure at the bottom opening from the reservoir is P_a+\rho g d, so the trapped air pushes upward on the water column with F_{\mathrm{up}}=A\left(P_a+\rho g d\right) and similarly pushes downward on the top of the water column with force F_{\mathrm{down}}=A P(x) Since the water column also has weight, F_{\text {weight }}=m g=\rho A xg, the net force is \begin{aligned} F_{\text {net }} & =F_{\text {up }}-F_{\text {air }}-F_{\text {weight }} \\ & =A\left(P_a+\rho g d\right)-A P(x)-\rho A x g \\ & =A\left[P_a+\rho g d-P(x)-\rho g x\right] . \end{aligned} Since m \ddot{x}=F_{\mathrm{net}}, then we have a simplified equation of motion, where viscous damping and the momentum flux associated with water are neglected. \rho A x \ddot{x} = A\left[P_a+\rho gd-P(x)-\rho gx\right] \tag{2} For the isothermal model, the trapped air obeys \begin{align} P(x)V(x) & =P_{\mathrm{eq}}V_{\mathrm{eq}}\\ P(x) & =P_{\mathrm{eq}}\frac{L-y}{L-x} \end{align} \tag{3} Next, we linearize around equilibrium P(x)=P_{\mathrm{eq}}\frac{L-y}{L-x} \tag{3} The area A cancels because both the trapped-air volume and the water-column mass are proportional to A.To obtain the natural frequency, write x(t)=y+\eta(t) where |\eta|\ll y. Linearizing Equation (2) about y and using Equation (3) gives \rho y \ddot{\eta} = -\left[\rho g+\frac{P_{\mathrm{eq}}}{L-y}\right]\eta Therefore, \ddot{\eta}+\omega_{\mathrm{th}}^2\eta=0 with \boxed{ \omega_{\mathrm{th}}^2 = \frac{g}{y} + \frac{P_{\mathrm{eq}}}{\rho y(L-y)} } \tag{4} and, using Equation (1), \boxed{ \omega_{\mathrm{th}}^2 = \frac{g}{y} + \frac{P_a+\rho g(d-y)}{\rho y(L-y)} } \tag{5} All lengths in Equation (5) must be expressed in SI units. The first term is the hydrostatic contribution, and the second term is the trapped-air spring contribution. The isothermal model predicts a strong dependence on the filling fraction y/L, especially because the air volume A(L-y) changes as the tube becomes more full.The data showed a systematic residual from the isothermal model, so we also considered the more general polytropic relation P(x)V(x)^\kappa=P_{\mathrm{eq}}V_{\mathrm{eq}}^\kappa In that case, P(x)=P_{\mathrm{eq}}\left(\frac{L-y}{L-x}\right)^\kappa and the same linearization gives \boxed{ \omega_{\kappa}^2 = \frac{g}{y} + \frac{\kappa\left[P_a+\rho g(d-y)\right]}{\rho y(L-y)} } \tag{6} Equation (5) is the special case \kappa=1. For air, the adiabatic limiting value is approximately \kappa=1.4. In this report, \kappa is treated as a fitted parameter inferred from the dataset, not as an independently known property of the apparatus.1.2 Experimental fit formThe videos were analyzed by tracking the meniscus position after the tube had been reclamped. The manual recommends setting the origin at the final equilibrium meniscus position and fitting the displacement to a damped cosine.Lab manual. The numerical fit used the closely related form z(t)=c+a e^{-bt}\cos(\omega_{\mathrm{exp}}t+\phi) \tag{7} The constant offset c absorbs small residual errors in the Tracker coordinate origin and does not affect the fitted angular frequency. The fitted angular frequency \omega_{\mathrm{exp}} is the parameter to be compared with Equation (5) and Equation (6).To include damping, I model the small oscillation about equilibrium as a linearly damped harmonic oscillator. After linearization, the displacement \eta(t)=x(t)-y is assumed to satisfy \ddot{\eta}+2\lambda\dot{\eta}+\omega_\kappa^2\eta=0, \tag{19} where \lambda is the exponential decay rate and \omega_\kappa is the undamped natural angular frequency predicted by the polytropic model. This damping term is introduced phenomenologically at the linearized level; it is not derived from the full fluid dynamics.To solve Eq. (19), write \eta(t)=e^{-\lambda t}u(t). Then \dot{\eta} = e^{-\lambda t}\left(\dot{u}-\lambda u\right), and \ddot{\eta} = e^{-\lambda t}\left(\ddot{u}-2\lambda\dot{u}+\lambda^2 u\right). Substituting these into Eq. (19) gives e^{-\lambda t}\left(\ddot{u}-2\lambda\dot{u}+\lambda^2 u\right) + 2\lambda e^{-\lambda t}\left(\dot{u}-\lambda u\right) + \omega_\kappa^2 e^{-\lambda t}u = 0. Factoring out e^{-\lambda t} and simplifying, \ddot{u}-2\lambda\dot{u}+\lambda^2 u +2\lambda\dot{u}-2\lambda^2 u +\omega_\kappa^2 u = 0, so \ddot{u}+(\omega_\kappa^2-\lambda^2)u=0. \tag{20} This is the equation of a simple harmonic oscillator. Therefore, for underdamped motion, \lambda<\omega_\kappa, the solution is u(t)=a\cos(\omega_{\mathrm{data}}t+\phi), where \omega_{\mathrm{data}}^2=\omega_\kappa^2-\lambda^2. \tag{21} Substituting back into \eta(t)=e^{-\lambda t}u(t) gives \eta(t)=a e^{-\lambda t}\cos(\omega_{\mathrm{data}}t+\phi). Since the Tracker origin may contain a small residual offset, the fitted coordinate is written as z(t)=z_0+a e^{-\lambda t}\cos(\omega_{\mathrm{data}}t+\phi), \tag{22} where z_0 is a small constant offset.Equation (21) can be written equivalently as \omega_\kappa=\sqrt{\omega_{\mathrm{data}}^2+\lambda^2}. \tag{23} Combining this result with the undamped polytropic prediction, \omega_\kappa^2 = \frac{g}{y} + \frac{\kappa\left[P_a+\rho g(d-y)\right]}{\rho y(L-y)}, gives the damped polytropic prediction for the measured angular frequency, \omega_{\mathrm{data},\kappa} = \sqrt{ \frac{g}{y} + \frac{\kappa\left[P_a+\rho g(d-y)\right]}{\rho y(L-y)} -\lambda^2 }. \tag{24} The corresponding damped isothermal prediction is the special case \kappa=1: \omega_{\mathrm{data,iso}} = \sqrt{ \frac{g}{y} + \frac{P_a+\rho g(d-y)}{\rho y(L-y)} -\lambda^2 }. \tag{25} In the data analysis, \lambda was obtained from the same damped-cosine fit used to determine \omega_{\mathrm{data}}. The damping correction in Eq. (23) was then checked using the fitted values of \lambda. Since this correction was much smaller than the systematic difference between the isothermal prediction and the measured frequencies, the main comparison uses \omega_{\mathrm{data}} directly against the undamped theory as a first approximation.
